title: HDB Loans for Second- and Third-time Flat Buyers
what_it_is: HDB Loans for Second- and Third-time Flat Buyers

sections.label: HDB loan limit and flexibility
sections.summary: The two-loan limit prevents excessive churning of HDB flats, though HDB may grant a third loan case-by-case to households with sufficient savings and steady incomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The limit of two concessionary loans also helps to ensure the stability of the resale market by preventing excessive churning of HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, HDB does exercise flexibility to assist households with a third HDB housing loan on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The households that receive these third loans are required to have sufficient savings and steady incomes to service the loan because this credit assessment is needed to ensure that households do not end up taking on more debt than they are able to afford.

sections.label: Third HDB loans granted
sections.summary: HDB provided a third loan to about 900 households last year, 75% non-concessionary and 25% concessionary, while assessing applicants to avoid over-stretching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Last year, it provided a third loan to about 900 households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: About 75% of these loans are on a non-concessionary basis – that means, market rate – and 25% are concessionary loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have said, HDB would want to help and assist applicants to buy a home but HDB is also wary of people who over-stretch, families who over-stretch themselves and end up with more debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not think we want that to happen either just for the pursuit of buying a home, over-stretching their finances and ending up with more debt than is prudent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, that remains the basis for which HDB will do its assessments but, generally, HDB will also be flexible in wanting to assist applicants to buy their own homes.
